# Manufacturing Award [MA000010]
## Find pay rates and entitlements
Use our tools and resources to:

- [find your award](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/employment-conditions/awards/awards-summary/ma000010-summary#find-your-award)
- [calculate pay rates, penalty rates and allowances](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/employment-conditions/awards/awards-summary/ma000010-summary#calculate-pay-rates-penalty-rates-and-allowances)
- [work out notice periods and redundancy pay](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/employment-conditions/awards/awards-summary/ma000010-summary#work-out-notice-periods-and-redundancy-pay)
- [fix a workplace problem](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/employment-conditions/awards/awards-summary/ma000010-summary#fix-a-workplace-problem).

### Find your award
If you’re not sure of your award, use our [Pay and Conditions Tool](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/pay-and-wages/pay-calculator).

Awards are also available from our [List of awards](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/employment-conditions/awards/list-of-awards) page.

### Calculate pay rates, penalty rates and allowances
You can calculate pay rates, penalty rates and allowances using our [Pay and Conditions Tool](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/pay-and-wages/pay-calculator).

Prefer a single document? You can also download the pay guide for your award from our [Pay guides](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/pay-and-wages/minimum-wages/pay-guides) page.

### Work out notice periods and redundancy pay
You can find out how much notice and redundancy pay is required under your award using our [Pay and Conditions Tool](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/ending-employment/notice-redundancy-calculator).

### Check your award entitlements
For many common awards, we have tailored information about rules on employment conditions like:

- [hours of work](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/employment-conditions/hours-of-work-breaks-and-rosters/hours-of-work)
- [breaks](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/employment-conditions/hours-of-work-breaks-and-rosters/breaks)
- [rosters](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/employment-conditions/hours-of-work-breaks-and-rosters/rosters)
- [right to disconnect](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/employment-conditions/right-to-disconnect).

results.title: Manufacturing Award 2020 [MA000010]: Pay Rates & Obligations
results.description:
If your business employs factory, production, or technical staff, you’re likely covered by the Manufacturing and Associated Industries and Occupations Award 2020 [MA000010].

The Fair Work Commission increased Manufacturing Award wages by 3.75% from 1 July 2025. Employers must now review classifications, allowances, and penalty rates to ensure staff are paid correctly and compliance standards are met.

This guide breaks down who the Award covers, how to classify employees, and what pay, leave, and penalty rules apply—so you can meet your obligations confidently and avoid costly back pay or Fair Work issues.

- The Manufacturing and Associated Industries and Occupations Award 2020 sets minimum pay rates, allowances, and work conditions for Australia’s manufacturing, engineering, and technical employees under the Fair Work Act 2009.
- Pay rates are reviewed annually by the Fair Work Commission. From 1 July 2025, wages increased by 3.75%.

## Award Basics
This Award sets the legal minimum pay rates, working hours, leave, and allowances for employees in the manufacturing and engineering sectors.

Apprentices, trainees, and juniors receive a percentage of the adult rate, which increases as they gain experience or age.

The clauses explain the rules around things like pay, hours, breaks, and leave. The schedules provide the detailed classification structure and the pay rates for each level.

## Pay Rates and Entitlements
The Manufacturing Awardsets minimum pay and work conditions for manufacturing, engineering, and production employees.

It covers ordinary hours, overtime, weekends, public holidays, allowances, and leave.

You can’t pay less than the minimum Manufacturing Award pay rates, but you can offer higher pay.

### Standard minimum base rates (adult full-time)
|  |  |  |  |
|-|-|-|-|
| **Classification** | **Typical role** | **Hourly rate** | **Weekly rate** |
| **C14** | Entry-level/basic factory hand | 24.28 | 922.70 |
| **C12** | Certificate II production worker | 25.85 | 982.40 |
| **C10** | Qualified tradesperson (Cert III) | 28.12 | 1,068.40 |
| **C7** | Advanced tradesperson/team leader | 30.68 | 1,165.70 |
| **C3** | Engineering associate / technical designer | 35.55 | 1,350.80 |
| **C1** | Professional engineer/scientist | 38.03 | 1,445.10 |
| *This information is current as of October 2025. It’s based on the Award, which was last updated 1 July 2025. |

## How To Determine Manufacturing Award Coverage
### Manufacturing Award: A practical example
- Her welders, doing skilled trade work, are classified under C10 and currently earn $28.12/hour.
- The machine operator doing routine production tasks fits the C12 classification and earns around $25.85/hour.

Emma pays her trades and production staff according to the Manufacturing Award’s minimum rates and penalty provisions, and her admin employee according to the Clerks Award.

## Resources and Links
### What’s the current minimum wage under the Manufacturing Award?
As of 1 July 2025, the minimum hourly rate for a C14-level employee under the Manufacturing Award is $24.28, with higher levels paid progressively more.
